Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Compliance affidavit filed by learned A.G.A. in relation to service of notice on respondent no. 2 is taken on record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 5.10.2023 and 21.10.2023 passed by the Special Judge S.C./S.T. Act, Bareilly.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as the learned AGA and perused the entire record.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He has not committed the present offence.

Further submitted that the Tasleem vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68056549/
1 victim was major at the time of alleged incident who lodged the present F.I.R. by concocting a false story on account of mutual dispute between both of them.

entities.text: Tasleem vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is allegation of committing rape with her by the appellant and F.I.R. was lodged on the same day but during medical examination no any internal or external injury was found on the person of the victim to show that rape was committed with her.

It is also submitted that in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. alleged that after incident she sat on the motorcycle of appellant from where he took her to some desolated place where she made noise at which people caught the appellant and handed over to the police but the appellant was arrested on 30.6.2023 as shown in the case diary, it also falsify the fact as disclosed by the victim before the learned Magistrate the he was caught by the the people on 29.6.2023.
The video has been said to be prepared by the appellant but there is nothing on record to show that such video was prepared by him.
There is no any other material on record to show the complicity of the appellant in the present case.
The Court below while passing the impugned order did not take into account the facts and evidence available on record in right perspective and erred in passing the same.
Appellant is in jail since 1.7.2023.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.
On the other hand, learned AGA opposing the prayer for bail.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellant Tasleem involved in Case Crime No. 399 of 2023, under Sections 376, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(V) SC/ST Act, P.S. Baheri, District Bareilly be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
